players.product: Custom data-center AI silicon (new entrant; hyperscaler custom-ASIC engagement)

quarterly_data.signal: Data-center AI software after the Modular acquisition (Chris Lattner, EVP of Advanced AI Software, who joined Qualcomm through the acquisition of Modular): Modular's unified stack (Mojo, MAX, Modular Cloud) now supports 'six different major architectures from six different hardware vendors', including data-center special-purpose accelerators; Modular has been 'bringing the stack to the Qualcomm Dragonfly family of data center accelerators', built on Qualcomm's NPU platform, and 'showed how we can deliver industry-leading performance on the system'. The stack is 'serving trillions of tokens in productions every few days'; Mojo 1.0 was released last month as production-ready and open-sourced under the Apache 2.0 license. Qualcomm is now bringing the Modular platform to its entire portfolio, including Snapdragon, and is partnering with Microsoft to deepen support for the Modular stack (native Mojo) on Windows.
quarterly_data.figure: six major architectures from six hardware vendors; Mojo 1.0 open-sourced (Apache 2.0)

quarterly_data.signal: PC business (Kedar Kondap, Qualcomm executive): 'more than 7,300 apps now run on Windows on Snapdragon'; more than 170 designs across every major PC manufacturer; more than 1,800 ecosystem devices tested for interoperability and compatibility; more than 12,000 stores across 120 global retailers carry the devices; more than 150,000 sellers trained. 'Starting with the Snapdragon X2 Series, Linux is officially supported on Snapdragon. Linux support with Debian will be available at the end of this year.' The HUMAIN Horizon Ultra AI PC (an agentic OS built on Linux, on Snapdragon X2 Elite) 'will be available in the first half of 2027'; ASUS is bringing Ubuntu to its Snapdragon X2 Series devices (Zenbook A14 and Zenbook A16) starting in the first half of next year; Google's Googlebook laptop has Snapdragon X Elite 'right at the center of it'. Kondap: 'Three operating systems, and Snapdragon powering all of them' (Windows, Googlebook, Linux).
quarterly_data.figure: more than 7,300 apps; more than 170 designs; Linux (Debian) support at the end of this year; HUMAIN Horizon Ultra AI PC in the first half of 2027

quarterly_data.signal: Personal AI wearables and named customers (Ziad, Qualcomm executive): Snapdragon AR1 and AR1+ are, per Qualcomm, 'the world's first personal AI platforms to support multi-model, 1-bit models', with 'many more Snapdragon platforms to follow'. Customers include 'a growing list of the top brands, hyperscalers, and more': Meta - 'Starting with the original Ray-Ban Stories glasses, Snapdragon working with Meta helped lay the foundation for the smart eyewear market'; Snap, whose Specs augmented reality glasses launched last week; Samsung (watches, XR and intelligent eyewear); and Google. Snapdragon START scaling program (Cameron Slaviero, Qualcomm software team lead): 'one of the smallest modules for AI glasses built on our Snapdragon AR1+ platform' plus an end-to-end glass/phone/cloud AI software platform; Ziad called the InspEx enterprise and medical eyewear family the 'First devices based on Start'. Qualcomm also previewed a personal AI pin reference design on the Snapdragon Wear Elite platform (standalone 5G connectivity, dual cameras; more to share next year) and announced the formation of the Personal AI Health Alliance.

Snapdragon Sound Elite Gen 2 launched - per Ziad 'the first premium audio platform purpose-built for the age of personal AI'. Andy (product manager, premium audio): 'we made it 30% smaller', 'we doubled the compute and AI performance', 'we cut the power consumption by 40%', with Qualcomm's 'first integrated Bluetooth and micropower Wi-Fi'; a new Snapdragon Sound Apps and Agents ecosystem of hearable apps (working with MicroEdge, Cinemo and Roon). Cleer is pioneering audio-plus-vision earbuds with Qualcomm, HP is 'developing an exciting new product based on the Snapdragon Sound Elite platform', and Qualcomm has been working closely with Bose on future generations of the platform.
quarterly_data.figure: 30% smaller; compute and AI performance doubled; power consumption cut by 40%
